chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Aamir ibn al-Simt, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) – similar to it.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ali ibn Ja'far ibn Ishaq al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The wine is from five: the juice from the grapes, the marinade from the raisins, the mead from the honey, the ale from the barley, and Al-Nabeez from the dates.
ai.seo_question: What are the five sources of wine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through prominent chains in al-Kafi, explicitly categorizes the five primary ingredients—grapes, raisins, honey, barley, and dates—that yield wine (khamr) according to Shia jurisprudence. It provides the essential botanical basis for distinguishing between specific types of intoxicants and their legal status, reinforcing the Prophet's definition which underpins the broader prohibition of intoxicants in Islamic law.
